findings.summary: Production readDoc keys the reuse lookup on (doc_kind, origin), not (role, origin) as the spec requires. deriveDocKind maps all three debater roles to doc_kind "argument", so the find() returns the same first-matching argument message for dr-debater-advocate, dr-debater-opponent and dr-debater-judge. When only some debater docs exist for an origin, the missing debaters are treated as already present: they are never spawned and never published, and their bodies are silently replaced by the one existing argument body. This directly violates W3 (only spawn the missing role) and corrupts the synthesizer inputs (prior_arguments and arguments become three copies of one argument).

W3 is not actually demonstrated against production-assembled deps, so W6 is unmet. Every W1-W4 case injects a hand-written readDoc mock that correctly discriminates on role, which the production implementation cannot do. The only tests exercising assembleGenerateDeps place a single doc in the fake bus (one report, or one non-matching argument), so the multi-argument role-collision path is never covered. Adding two distinct debater argument docs for the same origin and asserting the spawned role set would fail against the current production readDoc.

research.doc.v2 carries no role discriminator (DocV2 is doc_kind/digest/body/origin), so (role, origin) reuse is not derivable from the published payload alone for the three argument-producing roles. A correct fix needs a role-bearing signal on the doc message or a lookup keyed by the existing idempotency key dr-doc:${role}:${origin}; the current payload-shape scan cannot satisfy the spec key without one.

The W8 reachability declaration asserts role-discriminating reuse behavior (W1 and W3 rows) that only the injected mocks exhibit. Because the production readDoc cannot distinguish the three debater roles, the stated reason why each criterion is unreachable without the implementation does not hold for the production path.

In the resumed-synthesizer branch the anchor-check result is recomputed into anchorRate/anchorTail and then never used: the export sends the stored synthBody, which already contains its persisted head. The anchor-check runs purely for its side effects while the freshly derived rate and tail are discarded, leaving dead computation and duplicated anchor-check logic with the non-resumed branch.
